A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' energy-based diffusion and hybrid MCTS framework, renamed from T-SCEND to VFScale. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Maze and Sudoku experiments, including generalization results, inference-budget comparisons, loss ablations, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original Maze and Sudoku results and adds a denoising-quality diagnostic, training-time measurements, and a conventional-DDPM hMCTS experiment.

M1.justification: The principal losses, architectures, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged after matching the rename and relocation. However, v3 Appendix E explicitly adapts hMCTS to conventional noise-predicting DDPM, replacing the learned-energy reward with an external ground-truth negative-MSE reward. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Maze size-generalization coverage and SAT-Net-to-RRN Sudoku evaluation with fewer given digits. The appendix dataset specifications are retained. The new DDPM experiment uses the existing 15-by-15 Maze task, without introducing another dataset, population, or task requirement.

E2.justification: The original Du et al. training baseline, loss variants, plain MCTS, random search/BoN, DDPM, and untrained controls are retained. v1 Tables 10–11 survive as v3 Tables 11–12. The new DDPM-hMCTS experiment evaluates an extension of the proposed method against the already-used DDPM-BoN comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds an oracle negative-MSE protocol for DDPM-hMCTS and examines sample distances at denoising steps 0, 3, 6, and 9. Section 5 also newly describes Maze success as matching all 961 entries, while Appendices B.1/B.3 retain the earlier continuous-valid-path definition. This changes the reported metric description, but does not establish that the underlying evaluation was changed or rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 4 adds sample-distance distributions across denoising steps for the four training variants, and Appendix E tests hMCTS compatibility with conventional DDPM. The Sudoku performance-energy consistency analysis is removed. Existing loss ablations, noise-scale, inner-loop and MCTS-start sensitivity analyses, and qualitative cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed sets, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The new sample-distance histograms describe generated samples rather than uncertainty in repeated experimental estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces full-model Maze success at sizes 10/12/15 from 0.9922/0.9141/0.6562 to 0.7750/0.5391/0.2812. At N=161, reported Maze consistency changes from 0.3103 to 0.7300 for Original and from 0.4998 to 0.8371 for LRNCL-only; Sudoku consistency entries disappear. New diagnostics, timings, and DDPM-hMCTS results are added. Table 13 shows budget-dependent advantages, including worse performance than BoN at N=21 and equality at N=161. The headline hMCTS scores of 0.8828 and 0.4297 remain. Unclear protocol descriptions prevent interpreting the replaced values as established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the explicit constrained-optimization formulation and assumption that training samples are supported on a feasible set with a conditional input–solution formulation using J(c,x). The loss equations, operative search rule, consistency definition, and appendix regression mathematics remain substantively unchanged. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: v3 makes verifier-free intrinsic reasoning an explicit central contribution and drops the specific headline claim that KL regularization reduces adversarial sampling. The change is limited because v1 already used intrinsic energy and stated independence from external guidance. The principal training/search contributions and Maze/Sudoku headline outcomes remain.

C2.justification: v1 interprets poor oracle-guided sampling as evidence of adversarial sampling; v3 recasts the discussion around verifier misestimation and search-efficiency bottlenecks. Appendix E adds an applicability argument for conventional diffusion, conditional on an external verifier. The substantive limitations concerning parallelism, early node evaluation, linear regularization, and Gaussian branching are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.4 reports GPU/CPU resources and training times for the baseline and loss variants, including Maze baseline/full-model times of 2/6 hours and Sudoku times of 4/7 hours. Its stated timing budgets differ from the retained training tables, leaving their relationship unclear. The supplied repository target changes from t_scend to VFScale. Existing architecture and hyperparameter disclosures remain.

R1.justification: The controllable-generation and general MCTS discussion is replaced by positioning around diffusion reasoning and verifier-dependent test-time scaling. v3 adds Du et al. (2022), Yoon et al. (2025), verification research, and cognitive-reasoning references. It substantially reframes the distinction from Ma et al. (2025) around intrinsic verification rather than primarily improved training and search.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, problem setup, and experimental interpretation undergo extensive rewriting. LRNCL exposition becomes a numbered sequence, Algorithm 1 moves from the main text to Appendix A, and new appendix subsections reorganize the supporting material. These changes substantially revise the narrative beyond the method rename.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures and tables. Figure 1 is rearranged, the consistency table loses its Sudoku block, and new Figure 4 and Table 13 are introduced. v3 Table 2 redisplays existing oracle-comparison results, while appendix visualizations are retained and rearranged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides clearer stepwise exposition, additional denoising and DDPM evidence, and useful cost disclosures. However, Sudoku consistency evidence is removed, substantial reported scores are replaced without explaining their provenance, and the new Maze-success and timing descriptions do not align clearly with retained appendix definitions/settings. The DDPM results also support only a budget-dependent efficiency advantage. These benefits and unresolved empirical-clarity issues prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
